(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

derivations.claim: The deletion rule. From $e_i' F_i=q_i^{-2}F_ie_i'+1$ and $e_i'(1)=0$, induction on $r\ge1$ gives $e_i'(F_i^r)=(\sum_{s=0}^{r-1}q_i^{-2s})F_i^{r-1}=q_i^{-(r-1)}[r]_iF_i^{r-1}$. Dividing by the nonzero $[r]_i!$ yields $e_i'(F_i^{(r)})=q_i^{-(r-1)}F_i^{(r-1)}$. For $j\ne i$, the relation $e_i' F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'$ and $e_i'(1)=0$ give $e_i'(F_j^r)=0$, hence $e_i'(F_j^{(r)})=0$.

$e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: by [F3] it suffices to check a divided-power word $w=F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{j_m}^{(r_m)}$, by induction on $m$ using the twisted Leibniz rule of [F1] and the deletion rule of step 1.1: $e_i'(w)=e_i'(F_{j_1}^{(r_1)})w'+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}),h_i\rangle}F_{j_1}^{(r_1)}e_i'(w')$, where $w'$ is the restricted word, the first factor is $0$ or $q_i^{-(r_1-1)}F_i^{(r_1-1)}\in U_A^-$ by step 1.1, the scalar $q_i^{\langle-r_1\alpha_{j_1},h_i\rangle}=q_i^{-r_1a_{ij_1}}\in A$, and $e_i'(w')\in U_A^-$ by induction; products of divided powers lie in $U_A^-$. By [F1] linearity extends this to all of $U_A^-$.

Powers of the derivation on a string: if $u\in\ker e_i'$ then for $0\le n\le m$, $(e_i')^nF_i^{(m)}u=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u$. For $n=0$ this is clear; for the induction step, $e_i'(F_i^{(m-n)}u)=e_i'(F_i^{(m-n)})u+q_i^{-2(m-n)}F_i^{(m-n)}e_i'(u)=q_i^{-(m-n-1)}F_i^{(m-n-1)}u$, where the second summand vanishes because $e_i'u=0$; multiplying by $q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}$ gives the exponent $-(n+1)m+(n+1)(n+2)/2$ as required.

The projector: $P_i$ is well defined by [F2], and $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear. Consecutive terms cancel in $e_i'P_i$: applying $e_i'$ to the $n$-th term gives $(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}[e_i'(F_i^{(n)})(e_i')^n+q_i^{-2n}F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^{n+1}]=(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}[q_i^{-(n-1)}F_i^{(n-1)}(e_i')^n+q_i^{-2n}F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^{n+1}]$ by steps 1.1, 2.2, and the contribution of the second part of the $n$-th term cancels the first part of the $(n+1)$-st term because $-n(n-1)/2-2n=-n(n+1)/2-(n)$; the $n=0$ contribution of the second part is $(e_i')^1$ and equals the first part of the $n=1$ term, so $e_i'P_i=0$. If $e_i'x=0$ then $(e_i')^nx=0$ for $n\ge1$, so $P_ix=F_i^{(0)}(e_i')^0x=x$: $P_i$ fixes $\ker e_i'$ pointwise.

$P_i$ annihilates $F_i\ker e_i'$: for $u\in\ker e_i'$ and $m\ge1$, step 2.2 gives $(e_i')^n(F_i^{(m)}u)=q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u$ for $n\le m$, and $(e_i')^n(F_i^{(m)}u)=q_i^{-n(m-1)}F_i^{(m-1)}(e_i'u)=0$ for $n>m$ (the surviving term of the Leibniz expansion at the first step where the derivative reaches $u$); hence $P_i(F_i^{(m)}u)=\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}F_i^{(n)}q_i^{-nm+n(n+1)/2}F_i^{(m-n)}u=\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-nm+n}\binom{m}{n}_iF_i^{(m)}u=\bigl[\sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(m-1)}\binom{m}{n}_i\bigr]F_i^{(m)}u$, using [F4] for $F_i^{(n)}F_i^{(m-n)}$. By [F5] the bracket is $1$ for $m=0$ and $0$ for $m\ge1$; hence $P_i$ fixes $\ker e_i'$ and annihilates $F_i^{(m)}\ker e_i'$ for every $m\ge1$.

Decomposition and uniqueness: for $x\in U_q^-$ let $m$ be maximal with $(e_i')^mx\ne0$ (finite by [F2]) or $m=0$ if $e_i'x=0$, and put $x_m:=q_i^{m(m-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^mx$; then $e_i'x_m=q_i^{m(m-1)/2}e_i'P_i(e_i')^mx=0$ by step 3.1, and $x':=x-F_i^{(m)}x_m$ satisfies $(e_i')^mx'=(e_i')^mx-q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}x_m=0$ by step 2.2 and step 3.1, so $\operatorname{ord}(x')\le m-1$. Descending induction on $m$ therefore writes $x=\sum_{n}F_i^{(n)}x_n$ with $e_i'x_n=0$ and $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx$: at each stage the coefficient of the remainder agrees with the claimed formula because $P_i$ annihilates the subtracted strings $F_i^{(m-n)}x_m$ by step 3.2, so $P_i(e_i')^nx'=P_i(e_i')^nx$ for $n<m$. If also $x=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}y_n$ with $e_i' y_n=0$, subtract the two finite expansions and put $z_n:=x_n-y_n$. If some $z_n$ is nonzero, let $N$ be its largest index. Applying $(e_i')^N$ to $0=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}z_n$ gives $0=q_i^{-N(N-1)/2}z_N$ by step 2.2, a contradiction. Thus every $z_n=0$, proving uniqueness.

Integrality and conclusion: each $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx$ lies in $U_A^-$, because $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$ by step 2.1, every $(e_i')^nx$ is therefore in $U_A^-$, the coefficients $q_i^{\pm m(m-1)/2}$ and $(-1)^m$ lie in $A$, and each $F_i^{(m)}$ is a generator of $U_A^-$; hence the finite sum $P_i(\,\cdot\,)$ of the definition lies in $U_A^-$ on $U_A^-$. Consequently every string coefficient $x_n$ of an $x\in U_A^-$ is integral. For the projection claim, apply step 4.1 to the expansion of an arbitrary $y$: $F_iy=\sum_{n\ge1}[n]_iF_i^{(n)}y_{n-1}$ decomposes with all string coefficients in $\ker e_i'$ and zero $n=0$ coefficient, so $P_i(F_iy)=0$ by the formula; hence $U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ with $P_i$ the projection along $F_iU_q^-$, and $x_0=P_ix\in U_A^-$ whenever $x\in U_A^-$. Finally the string operators of (iii) are well defined by the uniqueness of the expansion, and they preserve $U_A^-$ because they only shift the divided-power labels $n\mapsto n\pm1$ of the integral coefficients $x_n\in U_A^-$. No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ was used anywhere.

boundaries.evidence: the projector series in (ii) terminates because e_i' is locally nilpotent, and step 4.1 chooses m=0 exactly when e_i'x=0, where the decomposition reads x=x_0 in ker e_i'.

The coefficient formula of step 4.1 is linear and gives all zero coefficients for x=0; its comparison-of-expansions argument proves that the zero vector has no nonzero finite primitive-string expansion.
the r=1 deletion rule e_i'(F_i)=1 is the base case of step 1.1, and the n=0 instance of step 2.2 reads F_i^{(m)}u for a single leading divided power.

only the rank-one letter F_i and the single derivation e_i' occur, so no a_ij degeneracy arises; the inverted Gauss identity used in the alternating sum of step 3.2 is quantified over all N>=0 including N=0.
step 2.2 covers n=m, the last surviving divided power, and step 3.2 separates n<=m from n>m; step 4.1 uses the maximal m with (e_i')^m x nonzero as the terminal index of the decomposition.

boundaries.reason: P_i is an explicit alternating series (step 3.1) and the maximal m of step 4.1 exists by local nilpotence without appeal to a maximality principle, so no choice is exercised.
the lemma proves preservation, decomposition and projection identities, not a biconditional; the uniqueness clause of (iii) is established directly in step 4.1.
there is no converse to verify, since the decomposition x=sum_m F_i^{(m)}x_m is constructed and shown unique in a single pass in step 4.1 rather than by two implications.

citations.quote:
A **free abelian group on a set $X$** is an abelian group $A(X)$ together with
a map $i:X\to A(X)$ such that, for every abelian group $B$ and every
function $u:X\to B$, there is a unique group homomorphism
$\widehat u:A(X)\to B$ satisfying

$$\widehat u\circ i=u.$$

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

A **free abelian group on a set $X$** is an abelian group $A(X)$ together with
a map $i:X\to A(X)$ such that, for every abelian group $B$ and every
function $u:X\to B$, there is a unique group homomorphism
$\widehat u:A(X)\to B$ satisfying

$$\widehat u\circ i=u.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, steps
3.1 and 4.1).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: Choosing a free basis $e_1,\dots$ of $P$, let $S$ be the finite set of basis elements occurring in the finitely many elements $\lambda_j,\alpha_i$, and put $X_f:=\bigoplus_{s\in S}\mathbb Ze_s$. Then $X_f$ is free of finite rank, contains all $\lambda_j$ and $\alpha_i$, and $P=X_f\oplus X_f'$ for the summand $X_f'$ spanned by the remaining basis elements, by [F1]. [...]

By [F2] the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is perfect, and the map $j$ is an isomorphism of $X_f$ onto the subgroup $\{j(x)\}$ of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$; hence $j$ is injective, so the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}=j(\alpha_i)$ are linearly independent (as the $\alpha_i$ are, [[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]). [...]

Transport of the module: grade $M^{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ as in (ii) and let $K_{(n,f)}$ act on $M_x$ by the scalar $q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}$, while $E_i,F_i$ act as before. This is well defined because $P=X_f\oplus X_f'$ and $M$ has no labels in $X_f'$ by step 1.1, so $M=\bigoplus_{x\in X_f}M_x$. [...]

Converse and equivalence: given an $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one module $N$ with labels in $j(X_f)$ (i.e. $N_\xi=0$ for $\xi\notin j(X_f)$), define $N^{\mathrm{old}}$ with the same underlying vector spaces and $N^{\mathrm{old}}_x:=N_{j(x)}$ for $x\in X_f$; [...]

Simultaneity: for a Verma module or highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ the support lies in $\lambda-Q_+$, and for a finite tensor product of such modules the labels are sums of labels, hence lie in $\sum_k(\lambda^{(k)}-Q_+)\subseteq(\sum_k\lambda^{(k)})-Q_+$; [...]

Rational decomposition: let $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes\mathbb Q$, so $\dim h_{\mathrm{aux}}=n+\operatorname{rank}X_f$, and let $\alpha\colon h_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Q^I$ be the evaluation $\alpha(y)_i=\langle\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}},y\rangle$. It is surjective because the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are linearly independent and the pairing is perfect; [...]

boundaries.evidence: the finite coordinate summand X_f is allowed to be zero when all lambda_j and alpha_i vanish; step 1.1 then returns the rank-zero lattice and the auxiliary datum collapses to the original one.
step 6.1 decomposes h_aux=H_min direct-sum Z with Z central, the locus where every label vanishes; the zero label lies in X_f by step 1.1, keeping the reconstruction K_h=q^{<x,h>} valid.
the rank-one case of X_f is the simplest instance of step 1.1, and step 3.1 checks the transported action on a single label x, including K_0 acting by the scalar q^0=1.

the possibility that the original pairing is not perfect is exactly what the auxiliary datum repairs: step 2.1 installs a perfect pairing on X_aux x Y_aux, and step 6.1 splits off the central obstruction Z.

boundaries.reason: the construction has no index range; it uses only the finiteness of the set S of basis elements in step 1.1, so no minimal or maximal parameter arises to check.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 selects a free basis of P and the finite set S of basis elements occurring in the lambda_j and alpha_i; the selection is finite and AC-free, and the pairing of step 2.1 is the determined dual basis.
step 4.1 proves the forward direction on the nose: transporting a P-graded module to the auxiliary datum and applying the inverse recipe returns the original module and its labels.
step 4.1 also proves the reverse direction, rebuilding the old K_h from the label and matching the E_i,F_i actions, while step 3.1 verifies well-definedness of the transported structure.

citations.quote:
Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$.

derivations.claim: For every $r\ge0$ one has $\psi(E_i^{(r)})=\psi(E_i)^r/\psi([r]_i!)=E_i^r/[r]_i!=E_i^{(r)}$ and $\psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)}$, since $\psi$ fixes $E_i,F_i$ and fixes the scalar $[r]_i!$ by [F2]; on the torus $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$. [...]

For $\tau$, which is anti-multiplicative, $\tau(E_i^{(r)})=\tau(E_i^r)/\tau([r]_i!)=\tau(E_i)^r/[r]_i!=F_i^r/[r]_i!=F_i^{(r)}$ by [F2], and symmetrically $\tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)}$; $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; [...]

Consequently each of $\psi,\tau$ sends every generator of $U_A$ into $U_A$ by steps 1.1 and 2.1, and sends scalars $a\in A$ into $A$ by [F2]. From [F3], an element of $U_A$ is a finite sum $\sum_ja_jg_{j,1}\cdots g_{j,m_j}$ with $a_j\in A$ and generators $g_{j,l}$; [...]

boundaries.evidence: the empty product 1 is fixed by both maps: step 3.1 extends the generatorwise computations of steps 1.1 and 2.1 over finite products, whose base case is 1.
semilinearity gives psi(0)=tau(0)=0, and bijectivity of the two restrictions in step 3.1 covers the zero element without a separate clause.
steps 1.1 and 2.1 verify the degree-one divided powers E_i and F_i together with K_h^{±1}; the coefficient case a=1 is fixed because psi and tau act on scalars by q->q^{-1}.

the toral binomial is the delicate generator: steps 1.1 and 2.1 check each factor K_iq_i^{c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{-c+s-1} and show the two sign changes cancel, which is where the semilinear twist could have failed.
each toral factor is a product over s=1..t with endpoint s=t, computed explicitly in steps 1.1 and 2.1; t=0 gives T_{i,c,0}=1, fixed by both maps.

boundaries.reason: both maps are defined on generators and extended by (anti)multiplicativity with an induction on the length of a generator product in step 3.1, so no choice principle is needed.
the claim is a pair of set equalities psi(U_A)=U_A and tau(U_A)=U_A, each proved by a single induction on generator products in step 3.1, not by an implication.
applying the maps twice checks the two inclusions of each equality as containment bookkeeping, and the Lemma asserts no separate converse implication.

citations.quote:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with Borel subalgebra
$U_q^{\ge0}=U_q^0U_q^+$ and negative half $U_q^-$
([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Fix
$\lambda\in P$ and let $\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)$ be the
**Borel character module** on which $K_h$ acts by the scalar
$q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}$ and every $E_i$ acts as $0$ (the character is a
well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism
$\chi_\lambda\colon U_q^{\ge0}\to\mathbb Q(q)$, Verification, step 1.1). The
**quantum Verma module** is the induced module

$$M(\lambda):=U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U_q^{\ge0}}\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda,$$

a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module, with distinguished vector
$v_\lambda:=1\otimes1$ ([[def-quotient-ring]] for the quotient/induction
conventions).

Then (Verification, steps 2.1 and 3.1):

(i) $M(\lambda)$ carries the **canonical $P$-label grading**
$M(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M(\lambda)_\mu$ with
$M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$ for $\nu\in Q_+$ and
$M(\lambda)_\mu=0$ otherwise; each $M(\lambda)_\mu$ is finite dimensional
(there are only finitely many words in the $F_i$ of a given root degree), and
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ is the highest line. With this
grading $M(\lambda)$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and $v_\lambda$ is a highest
weight vector: $K_hv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v_\lambda$,
$E_iv_\lambda=0$, $M(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.

(ii) (Universal property) For every left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $V$ and every
$v\in V$ with $K_hv=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v$ and $E_iv=0$ for all $h,i$
there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with
$v_\lambda\mapsto v$; if $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is cyclic, this map is
surjective. When $V$ is a $P$-graded type-one module and $v\in V_\lambda$, the
map is grading-preserving.

(iii) The sum $N(\lambda)$ of all proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$ is a
proper graded submodule, and

$$L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$$

is the **simple highest weight quotient**: it has no nonzero proper graded
submodule, and it is the unique simple graded quotient of $M(\lambda)$ up to
isomorphism ([[def-submodule]]). Thus the maximal proper submodule occurring
here is the sum of *all* proper graded submodules, not an arbitrarily chosen
maximal one; no choice is used.

If the pairing separates $P$, then every submodule of $M(\lambda)$ is graded,
$N(\lambda)$ is the unique maximal proper submodule, and $L(\lambda)$ is the
ordinary simple (not only graded-simple) quotient: this is the usual simple
weight-module quotient of the Verma module over a separating torus
(Verification, step 4.1).

The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`
identifies $N(\lambda)$ with the radical of the normalized Verma contravariant
form and gives the canonical normalized form on $L(\lambda)$; for $\lambda$
dominant integral, the existence theorem
`thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique` proves the
ordinary simplicity and the universal integrable conclusions. Both are
declared obligations of those later items, not assumptions here.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with Borel subalgebra
$U_q^{\ge0}=U_q^0U_q^+$ and negative half $U_q^-$
([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Fix
$\lambda\in P$ and let $\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)$ be the
**Borel character module** on which $K_h$ acts by the scalar
$q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}$ and every $E_i$ acts as $0$ (the character is a
well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism
$\chi_\lambda\colon U_q^{\ge0}\to\mathbb Q(q)$, Verification, step 1.1). The
**quantum Verma module** is the induced module

$$M(\lambda):=U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U_q^{\ge0}}\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda,$$

a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module, with distinguished vector
$v_\lambda:=1\otimes1$ ([[def-quotient-ring]] for the quotient/induction
conventions).

Then (Verification, steps 2.1 and 3.1):

(i) $M(\lambda)$ carries the **canonical $P$-label grading**
$M(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M(\lambda)_\mu$ with
$M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$ for $\nu\in Q_+$ and
$M(\lambda)_\mu=0$ otherwise; each $M(\lambda)_\mu$ is finite dimensional
(there are only finitely many words in the $F_i$ of a given root degree), and
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ is the highest line. With this
grading $M(\lambda)$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and $v_\lambda$ is a highest
weight vector: $K_hv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v_\lambda$,
$E_iv_\lambda=0$, $M(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.

(ii) (Universal property) For every left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $V$ and every
$v\in V$ with $K_hv=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v$ and $E_iv=0$ for all $h,i$
there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with
$v_\lambda\mapsto v$; if $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is cyclic, this map is
surjective. When $V$ is a $P$-graded type-one module and $v\in V_\lambda$, the
map is grading-preserving.

(iii) The sum $N(\lambda)$ of all proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$ is a
proper graded submodule, and

$$L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$$

is the **simple highest weight quotient**: it has no nonzero proper graded
submodule, and it is the unique simple graded quotient of $M(\lambda)$ up to
isomorphism ([[def-submodule]]). Thus the maximal proper submodule occurring
here is the sum of *all* proper graded submodules, not an arbitrarily chosen
maximal one; no choice is used.

If the pairing separates $P$, then every submodule of $M(\lambda)$ is graded,
$N(\lambda)$ is the unique maximal proper submodule, and $L(\lambda)$ is the
ordinary simple (not only graded-simple) quotient: this is the usual simple
weight-module quotient of the Verma module over a separating torus
(Verification, step 4.1).

The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`
identifies $N(\lambda)$ with the radical of the normalized Verma contravariant
form and gives the canonical normalized form on $L(\lambda)$; for $\lambda$
dominant integral, the existence theorem
`thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique` proves the
ordinary simplicity and the universal integrable conclusions. Both are
declared obligations of those later items, not assumptions here.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Rank-one norms. Write $N_r:=B(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)$ and $m=m_i$. For $r\ge1$ use contravariance with $x=F_i$: since $F_iF_i^{(r-1)}=[r]_iF_i^{(r)}$ [F6], $N_r=[r]_i^{-1}B(F_iF_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)=[r]_i^{-1}B(F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,\sigma(F_i)F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)=[r]_i^{-1}q_i^{-1}B(F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,K_iE_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)$. By [F5], $E_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda=F_i^{(r-1)}T_{i,1-r,1}v_\lambda=F_i^{(r-1)}[m-r+1]_iv_\lambda$, so $K_iE_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda=[m-r+1]_iq_i^{m-2(r-1)}F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda$ and $N_r=[r]_i^{-1}q_i^{m-2r+1}[m-r+1]_iN_{r-1}$. With $N_0=1$, induction gives $N_r=\prod_{k=1}^{r}q_i^{m-2k+1}\frac{[m-k+1]_i}{[k]_i}=q_i^{rm-r^2}\frac{[m]_i\cdots[m-r+1]_i}{[1]_i\cdots[r]_i}=q_i^{r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_i$, since $\sum_{k=1}^{r}(m-2k+1)=rm-r^2$; when $r>m$ the factor $[m-r+1]_i=0$ appears and the product vanishes, and $\binom{m}{r}_i=0$ by [F6]. For $r=m_i+1$ this gives $N_{m_i+1}=0$; moreover for any word $w$ of degree $-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$ one has $w=cF_i^{(m_i+1)}$ because $U_q^-[-(m_i+1)\alpha_i]$ is spanned by the single word $F_i^{m_i+1}$, so $B(F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda,wv_\lambda)=0$ for all $w$, i.e. $F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda\in\operatorname{rad}B=N(\lambda)$ by step 4.1.

Ordinary simplicity. Let $V$ be the quotient of the statement and $0
e W\subseteq V$ an ordinary submodule. Choose $0
e x\in W$ and write $x=\sum_jx_j$ with nonzero homogeneous components of distinct labels $\mu_j\in\lambda-Q_+$. Choose a minimal label $\mu_j$ in this finite support. Homogeneity and nondegeneracy give a homogeneous $b\in U_q^-[-(\lambda-\mu_j)]$ with $B(x_j,b ar v_\lambda)
e0$. The vector $y:=\sigma(b)x$ belongs to $W$. For $k
e j$, $\sigma(b)x_k$ would have label $\lambda+\mu_k-\mu_j$, which cannot lie in $\lambda-Q_+$: membership would imply $\mu_k<\mu_j$, contradicting minimality. Thus $y=\sigma(b)x_j\in V_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q) ar v_\lambda$, and $B(y, ar v_\lambda)=B(x_j,b ar v_\lambda)
e0$. Hence $W$ contains $ ar v_\lambda$ and equals its cyclic module $V$. This proves ordinary simplicity without taking homogeneous components inside $W$.

Integrality. Let $\lambda$ be integral and $a,b\in U_A^-$. By the stability computation of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]] (applied to $\sigma$ in place of the two involutions named there: $\sigma(E_i^{(r)})=q_i^{r^2}F_i^{(r)}K_i^{-r}$ and $\sigma(F_i^{(r)})=q_i^{-r^2}K_i^rE_i^{(r)}$ lie in $U_A$, and $\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}$), one has $\sigma(a)b\in U_A$. Write $\sigma(a)b$ in the triangular spanning form $\sigma(a)b=\sum_tb_tu_tc_t$ with $b_t\in U_A^-$, $u_t\in U_A^0$, $c_t\in U_A^+$ ([[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] (iv)). Then $\sigma(a)bv_\lambda=\sum_t\epsilon_t\chi_\lambda(u_t)b_tv_\lambda$ with $\epsilon_t$ the augmentation of $c_t$, so $\eta(\sigma(a)b)=\sum_t\epsilon_t\chi_\lambda(u_t)\varepsilon(b_t)$ with $\varepsilon$ the augmentation of $U_A^-$: each of these three factors lies in $A$, because $\varepsilon(U_A^\pm)\subseteq A$, $\chi_\lambda(K_h)=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\in A$ and $\chi_\lambda(T_{i,c,t})=\left[\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+c\ \mathrm{choose}\ t\right]_i$, a Gaussian binomial with integer upper entry, which is an integer Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ by [F6] (the negative upper entry is handled by the finite product formula $[x]_i$ and the Gaussian quotient identities). Hence $B(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda)=\eta(\sigma(a)b)\in A$, which is (v). No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ and no $A$-valuedness of the negative-half Kashiwara form is claimed. This completes the construction and the proof.
