$M_A=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}(M_A\cap M_\mu)$ be a $U_A$-stable $A$-submodule that
is graded in the *lattice's own* sense, i.e. it is the direct sum of its
intersections with the label spaces. Then, on $M_A\otimes_Ak$, the operators
induced by $E_i,F_i$ (and all of $U_A$) satisfy: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$ for
every $h\in P^{\vee}$; $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acts on the image of $M_A\cap M_\mu$ by
the integer $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$; and
$[\bar E_i,\bar F_j]=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar E_j]=a_{ij}\bar E_j$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar F_j]=-a_{ij}\bar F_j$, where $\bar H_i$ acts on the image of
$M_A\cap M_\mu$ by the integer $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

The grading hypothesis in (b) is a real hypothesis on the lattice: it is not
inferred from the mere fact that $M_A$ spans a weight module. All divisions
that occur are performed inside the DVR
$R=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}$ (units $[r]_i!$ and $(q_i-q_i^{-1})$); no vanishing
denominator $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is substituted by $q=1$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $I=\{1\}$, $A=(2)$, so that $U_q(\mathfrak g)=U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with
generators $E,F,K^{\pm1}$ and $q_1=q$, and let $m\in\mathbb Z$; write
$\lambda$ for the weight with $\lambda(h_1)=m$ and
$[t]:=[t]_{1}=(q^{t}-q^{-t})/(q-q^{-1})$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]],
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

The quantum Verma module $M(m)=M(\lambda)$ has $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis
$\{v_t:=F^tv_0\}_{t\ge0}$ with $v_0=v_\lambda$ and weights $m-2t$, and the
actions are
$$Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t,\qquad Fv_t=v_{t+1},\qquad Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}\ \ (t\ge1),\qquad Ev_0=0$$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]), and:

(a) if $m\ge0$, the submodule generated by $F^{m+1}v_0$ is
$\bigoplus_{t\ge m+1}\mathbb Q(q)v_t$, and the quotient
$\tilde L(m)=M(m)/U_q(\mathfrak g)F^{m+1}v_0$ is the $(m+1)$-dimensional simple
module with basis $v_0,\dots,v_m$, $Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t$,
$Fv_t=[t+1]v_{t+1}$, $Ev_t=[m-t+1]v_{t-1}$; for $m=0$ this is the trivial
one-dimensional module;

(b) if $m=-1$, then $[m-t+1]=[-t]=-[t]\ne0$ for every $t\ge1$, so $M(-1)$ is
irreducible, infinite-dimensional and not integrable: the simple module
$L(-1)$ has a non-dominant, non-integral highest weight;

(c) for every $m<0$, $[m-t+1]$ vanishes only at the nonpositive integer
$t=m+1\le0$, so as in (b) $M(m)$ is irreducible, infinite-dimensional and not
integrable; the dominance hypothesis $m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ in
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] cannot be
relaxed.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$,
$U_A$ the integral form of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], and $k$
a characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$. Let
$\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ be the classical Lie algebra presented by
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots
([[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]).

(a) **Halves.** $U_A^\pm\otimes_Ak\cong U(\mathfrak n^\pm)_k$ by
$F_i\mapsto f_i$, respectively $E_i\mapsto e_i$.

(b) **Positive quotient.** The quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to
$U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$; in it $\bar H_i=\bar T_{i,0,1}$ is the
classical coroot generator, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$, and the positive
toral quotient is $k[H_i:i\in I]$ with kernel exactly
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$.

(c) **Operator form.** On every $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice the quotient
action of (b) is automatic: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$, the $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ act by
the integer binomials $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$, and all classical
Cartan and Serre operator relations hold, without any unproved global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness.

(d) **Boundaries.** The unquotiented specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$ is *not*
identified with $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$: it retains toral characters,
as the integral $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-representation with $E=F=0$, $K=-1$ shows.
Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on
label-graded modules; they are not fabricated as generators of the toral
integral form, and direct substitution $q=1$ into vanishing denominators
$q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed anywhere in this comparison.

Let $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ be the rank-one Cartan datum with $\lambda(h_1)=m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$,
and let $L(m)$ be the explicit simple module with basis $v_0,\dots,v_m$,
$Kv_t=q^{m-2t}v_t$, $Fv_t=[t+1]_qv_{t+1}$,
$Ev_t=[m-t+1]_qv_{t-1}$
([[ex-quantum-verma-and-simple-modules-for-sl-two]],
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let
$V_A=\sum_{t=0}^mAF^{(t)}v_0\subseteq L(m)$ be the lattice generated by the
highest weight vector under the divided powers of the integral form $U_A$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic $0$, made an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$, and put
$\bar V=V_A\otimes_Ak$.

Then $V_A$ is free over $A$ with basis $F^{(t)}v_0$ ($0\le t\le m$), and
$\bar V$ is a $k$-vector space of dimension $m+1$ with basis the images
$\bar v_t$ on which
$$\bar K=1,\qquad \bar F\bar v_t=(t+1)\bar v_{t+1},\qquad \bar E\bar v_t=(m-t+1)\bar v_{t-1},\qquad \bar T_{0,1}\bar v_t=(m-2t)\bar v_t,$$
with $\bar v_{-1}=\bar v_{m+1}=0$. This is exactly the classical
$(m+1)$-dimensional simple representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ on the coroot
basis: $\bar T_{0,1}$ is the Cartan generator $h$ acting by the weight $m-2t$,
and $\bar E,\bar F$ are the classical raising and lowering matrices, so the
weight multiplicities are $\dim_k\bar V_\mu=1$ for $\mu=m,m-2,\dots,-m$ and $0$
otherwise. For $m=2$ the specialized matrices are
$\bar E\bar v_0=0$, $\bar E\bar v_1=2\bar v_0$, $\bar E\bar v_2=\bar v_1$ and
$\bar F\bar v_0=\bar v_1$, $\bar F\bar v_1=2\bar v_2$, $\bar F\bar v_2=0$, with
$\bar T_{0,1}=\operatorname{diag}(2,0,-2)$, the standard adjoint-type triple.

derivations.claim: The element and its two evaluations. Let $x=T_{0,1}=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$. By [F1], $x\in U_A$ and on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ it acts by the scalar $[\mu(h_1)]_q$, whose value at $q=1$ is the integer $\mu(h_1)$. [...]

Explicit witness on $L(1)$. By [F2], in the two-dimensional module $L(1)$ the element $K$ acts as $\operatorname{diag}(q,q^{-1})$ and $x=T_{0,1}$ acts as $\operatorname{diag}([1]_q,[-1]_q)=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, a nonzero operator. [...]

Further witnesses. (i) The Gaussian integers: $[m]_q=\frac{q^m-q^{-m}}{q-q^{-1}}$ has numerator and denominator vanishing at $q=1$ for every $m\ne0$, while the correct specialization is the integer $m$; the same applies to the coefficient $\binom{m}{r}_q$ of the divided-power multiplication, whose naive $q=1$ value is $0/0$ whereas the correct value is the ordinary binomial. [...]

The correct statement. By [F4], specialization is the base change $U_A\otimes_Ak$ with $q\mapsto1$: it is defined on elements of the integral form (and on operator matrices on graded lattices, whose entries are Laurent polynomials), and the cancellations in Steps 1.1-1.3 are performed inside $U_A$ before any reduction. [...]

boundaries.evidence: the counterexample concerns nonempty rational expressions; step 1.1 already shows the vacuous feature of separate substitution, both numerator and denominator becoming undefined, so no empty-word case is available to test the false rule.

step 1.1 exhibits the 0/0 phenomenon and step 1.2 shows the true specialized operator is nonzero, diag(1,-1) on L(1); step 1.3 records the Gaussian-integer witnesses where the denominator vanishes while the correct value m is nonzero.
step 1.2 uses the first nontrivial module L(1) and step 1.3 the Gaussian integer [1]_q=1; the surviving K-character of the counterexample is the value -1 of K on the second weight of L(1).

the whole example is the degenerate case of a rational expression whose denominator vanishes at q=1; step 2.1 states the correct procedure, base change of the integral form, which avoids substituting into vanishing denominators.
step 1.1 evaluates the scalar [mu(h_1)]_q at both generic mu and at q=1, and step 1.3 treats m=0 and m!=0 of the Gaussian integer, the two ends of the vanishing dichotomy.

boundaries.reason: all witnesses are explicit elements and matrices; the counterexample selects nothing, and its conclusion is a failure statement rather than a construction requiring a principle.
a counterexample refutes a stated rule rather than proving a biconditional; the forward reading of the false rule is refuted in step 1.1 and the discussion of what remains true is step 2.1.
no converse is at issue: step 2.1 records the correct specialization statement, which is a different claim, and the example does not assert an equivalence between substitution rules.
